frontmatter.release_note: A video's TMDB credits now create real Person records — with linked roles and downloaded headshots — for its cast and crew, not just flat actor/director text.
A tag spelling you've blocked is no longer added as a multi-word tag's automatic dashed alias.

Every person, studio, tag, film and video now carries a copyable reference like `film:42`; films can be aliased and renamed like everything else; a film's files can carry an edition (Theatrical, Final Cut) read from the file or set by you; and a name can be shown one way while the file keeps another.

A provider that says two of your people are the same record now shows up in the Duplicates queue, ranked above the name-guesses and labelled with who said it — and a mis-picked entity in the enrich screen queues the pair instead of silently dropping the identity write.

The Duplicates queue no longer fills up with pairs whose only link is a provider-supplied alternate name. The Aliases panel now says which person or studio already holds a skipped name, and links to them.

frontmatter.profile: ui                  # UX change, behavior unchanged — the media title's rename field
frontmatter.release_note: Renaming a media item with a long title now shows the whole title while you edit it. The field spans the header, wraps onto more lines as needed, and uses the title's own type.

Files that are parts of one media can now carry a part number — `{part-2}` in the filename or a container tag — and show it on cards, the media page, film lists and queue rows, so three files enriched with the same provider entry stay tellable apart.

The skin is now the instance's identity — the owner picks it once on the new Appearance tab and every viewer sees it; an owner can also declare a custom palette (five colors on top of Cinémathèque) in holodex.yaml.
A cast member credited on the file under an alias now appears once in the writeback dialog, under their own name, instead of beside it.

frontmatter.release_note: Any video grid — browse, a person, tag, studio or film — can now be played straight through or shuffled with one press, and saved as a smart playlist that picks up newly matching videos on its own.

A film's description now sits at the top of the right-hand column with its tags, reads the same for the owner and for visitors, and the owner edits its source from a pencil beside the heading instead of a second copy lower down.

Long text — the media Overview, a person's Bio, a film's description — now reads the same everywhere and for everyone (small muted prose, clamped with the expand chevron), and the media Overview gains a pencil beside the heading that opens the source editor.

Video playlists — save the browse view you're looking at as a playlist, or add a video to one from its page; playlists are private until you make them public, and play through item to item (Picture-in-Picture included).

frontmatter.profile: backend             # behavior with no UI surface — a writeback queue id-reuse bug fix
frontmatter.release_note: Each write to a file now saves its own copy of the values it replaces, so Revert restores exactly what that write changed. Before, a write that came right after another could skip saving its copy, and Revert then mixed the two writes.

The media page now keeps tracking a file write until it finishes, however long it takes — the "writing to file" badge clears and the poster refreshes on its own instead of sticking until a reload after a slow (multi-GB) write.

If the server refuses a status check while the media page is tracking a file write (for example the video was removed or re-indexed mid-write), the page now recovers cleanly instead of leaving the "writing to file" badge stuck until you navigate away.

nodes.label: ADR-070: Canary Release Candidate + Retag Promotion
nodes.norm_label: adr-070: canary release candidate + retag promotion
nodes.rationale: Rebuilding the image again at release time risked shipping bits different from what was canaried, so a v* release instead retags the already-built, already-scanned sha-<short> digest from main. scripts/resolve-release-digest.mjs asserts ancestry to the tagged commit before promoting, guaranteeing released bits are byte-identical to the release candidate that was canaried.

nodes.label: HOLODEX-173/220 draft-PR guardrail incident
nodes.rationale: Standalone gate-artifact PRs (spec/ADR/design-handoff/worklog, e.g. #131/#137/#139/#181) were opened non-draft and each independently fired the Done transition on merge, cascading to Released on the next deploy, even though a docs-only merge can't be the PR that finishes an epic's implementation. Fixed by a 'Check changed paths' step that skips the Done transition when every changed file is under docs/**.

nodes.label: Branch↔Jira linkage
nodes.rationale: GitHub-for-Jira only links branches/PRs/builds/deployments to an issue when the issue key substring is present in the branch name. In Progress has no server-side event, so the agent fires it via direct Jira REST at branch-rename; CI fires In Review (PR marked ready), Done (merge), and Released (ghcr deploy) via direct REST calls rather than the metered Jira Automation Free-plan quota.

nodes.label: Core resolver model (baseline / enrichment / curation / decisions)
nodes.norm_label: core resolver model (baseline / enrichment / curation / decisions)
nodes.rationale: The file layer is baseline/default truth; provider enrichment is an additive shadow never flattened into the file layer; the pure resolver is the sole merge point; standing per-field source decisions plus curation override precedence at resolve time; Person and Studio ride the same decision model as entity-generic BaselineSource.

nodes.label: QA all three skins rule
nodes.rationale: Regressions routinely appear in only one skin (Cinémathèque, Broadcast, Brutalist), so every UI change must be eyeballed in all three, with fonts loading offline and loading/empty/error/grid states themed.

nodes.label: Tokens-only styling rule
nodes.rationale: Hardcoded palette/radius values won't react to skin switching, so all component styling must route through semantic CSS-variable-backed Tailwind utilities (bg-bg, text-ink, rounded-theme, etc); skin-specific flourishes are gated in app.css by [data-theme], not per-component markup.

nodes.label: Append-only migrations rule
nodes.rationale: golang-migrate has no auto-rollback, so a shipped migration is never edited — a new sequential NNNN_name.up.sql plus matching .down.sql is added instead.

nodes.label: Sidecar HTTP-only boundary rule
nodes.rationale: providers/tmdb is a standalone sidecar in the same Go module that must not import internal/*; it talks to core only over a versioned HTTP protocol (/healthz, /describe, /resolve, /enrich), keeping providers swappable without coupling to core internals.
